name: Terror
label: Victory Records
lede: A Buffalo lifer who had quit music moved to Los Angeles, got pulled into a band built from Carry On's leftovers, and by the band's own count has played well over 3,000 shows since.

eras.title: The Buffalo kid who quit, then didn't
eras.text: Scott Vogel had fronted three Buffalo bands that all broke up just as they got going, the last of them on Victory Records. He gave up on music and moved west, and Los Angeles hardcore handed him a new band within months.

years.h: Scott Vogel turns down 100 Demons and moves to Los Angeles
years.p: After Slugfest, Despair and Buried Alive, Vogel says he had quit music. He declines an offer to sing for 100 Demons and heads west.
years.xp:
Buried Alive had been on Victory Records, with The Death of Your Perfect World in 1999 and Last Rites in 2001. Vogel has described himself in those years as someone who only cared about hardcore and pushed everyone around him.

A friend then played him the LA band Carry On. When Carry On broke up and its members regrouped, they asked Vogel to sing.

years.h: Terror forms from ex-members of Carry On
years.p: Scott Vogel sings, ex-Carry On guitarist Todd Jones plays guitar, Nick Jett drums and Matt Smith plays bass. The name Terror comes in April, after the first shows are booked.

years.h: First show: opening for Diehard Youth at Pat's Warehouse, Ventura
years.p: Terror's first gig is an opening slot in Ventura, California. By mid-May the band is opening West Coast dates for Death Threat, American Nightmare and Striking Distance.

years.h: Richard Thurston joins on bass; Terror tours with Eighteen Visions
years.p: Terror becomes a five-piece after two demos, 4 Song Demo and Don't Need Your Help, and spends the fall on the road with Eighteen Visions.

years.h: Carl Schwartz replaces Richard Thurston on bass
years.p: Schwartz plays bass in Terror until the end of 2005.

years.h: Lowest of the Low on Bridge 9
years.p: Terror's first EP comes out on Boston's Bridge 9, along with the live album Life & Death. That spring the band tours Europe with Biohazard and Caliban.

eras.title: One with the underdogs
eras.text: Terror's debut album made the band a draw across the hardcore and metal tour circuit, from Sounds of the Underground to co-headlining with Hatebreed. Vogel's spine started to complain, and the founding guitarist moved on.

years.src: Wikipedia: Terror · Wikipedia: One with the Underdogs
years.h: One with the Underdogs sells over 40,000
years.p: Recorded at Sound City in Van Nuys and produced by the band for Trustkill, with Hatebreed's Jamey Jasta and Madball's Freddy Cricien guesting. It reaches number 28 on Independent Albums.

years.h: Scott Vogel's neck and back force Terror to cancel shows
years.p: Disc problems in Vogel's neck and back cancel several dates. By November he's back, co-headlining the US with [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]].

years.h: Terror on Sounds of the Underground with Lamb of God
years.p: Terror joins Lamb of God, Unearth and [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] on the traveling metal and hardcore package, and headlines North America with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]] in support.

years.h: Carl Schwartz leaves Terror for First Blood
years.p: Schwartz quits to play in First Blood full-time. Jonathan Buske takes over bass in March 2006.

years.src: Wikipedia: Terror · Wikipedia: Always the Hard Way
years.h: Always the Hard Way hits 10 on Heatseekers
years.p: Zeuss produces at Planet Z in Massachusetts. Leeway's Eddie Sutton sings on So Close to Defeat and rappers Murs and Mr. Dibbs appear on an interlude.
years.xp: It reached number 10 on Billboard's Heatseekers and 19 on Top Independent Albums. Terror spent the summer on Sounds of the Underground with As I Lay Dying, In Flames and Trivium, and made its first Persistence tour run with [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

years.h: Former Terror guitarist Todd Jones starts Nails
years.p: Todd Jones, who founded Terror with Scott Vogel, forms the grind-heavy [[Nails|a7d9c5f6-751d-4ea5-bf6d-39f1751d44a1]] and fronts it on guitar and vocals.

years.h: The Damned, the Shamed on Century Media
years.p: Terror's third album moves the band to the metal label Century Media. Bassist Jonathan Buske leaves in September.

eras.title: Keeping the faith through the churn
eras.text: New guitarist, new bassist, and a band that barely stopped touring: Asia, Australia, Europe. The line-up that settled here would make the next three albums together.

years.h: Jordan Posner replaces Doug Weber; David Wood joins on bass
years.p: Posner steps in on guitar as a temporary fix and stays for good. Wood takes over bass the same year.

years.h: Keepers of the Faith, about 2,500 sold in week one
years.p: Terror's fourth album, on Century Media. The same year Bridge 9 releases No Regrets, No Shame, filmed at the Showcase Theater in Corona, California in 2003.

years.h: Terror headlines Hell on Earth and Rebellion
years.p: Every Time I Die and All Shall Perish support on Hell on Earth; [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] and Death Before Dishonor join the Rebellion tour.

years.h: Terror cancels its Czech show in support of Randy Blythe
years.p: During the Persistence Tour, Terror pulls its Czech Republic date in support of Lamb of God singer Randy Blythe, then facing a manslaughter case in Prague.

eras.title: Three straight years on Victory
eras.text: Terror signed to the label that had released Vogel's Buried Alive a decade earlier. Live by the Code became the band's only Billboard 200 entry, and then Vogel's back gave out, twice.

years.h: Terror signs to Victory Records
years.p: Victory, which had released Scott Vogel's Buried Alive, takes Terror's CDs; Reaper Records does the vinyl.

years.cap: Live by the Code, Victory Records, 2013
years.h: Live by the Code, produced by New Found Glory's Chad Gilbert
years.p: Eleven songs in under 27 minutes. It enters the Billboard 200 at 145 with about 3,200 sold, Terror's only appearance on that chart, and tops Heatseekers.
years.xp: Vogel called it the dirtiest, rawest, most hardcore record the band had made since its early releases. The line-up was Vogel, Jordan Posner, Martin Stewart, David Wood and Nick Jett. Six songs got videos, from Live by the Code to Cold Truth.

years.h: Terror co-headlines Persistence with Suicidal Tendencies
years.p: Terror also plays the Vans Warped Tour and tours with Stick to Your Guns and Hundredth, while Defiant Music reissues its first three records.

years.h: The 25th Hour: 14 songs in under 23 minutes
years.p: Terror's second Victory album, recorded in January 2015 by Paul Miner and produced by Ben Cook. It reaches 8 on Top Hard Rock Albums and 46 in Germany.
years.xp: Andrew Kline of [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] was among the gang vocalists. In June 2015 a disc injury in Vogel's back cancelled the band's immediate tour plans; they were back out in the fall with [[Code Orange|b87d5807-c37a-4d0e-a53c-9cdf6bc6caa1]].

years.h: Scott Vogel needs back surgery and Terror cancels everything
years.p: Terror headlines The Life & Death Tour with Power Trip and Harm's Way, until another spinal injury forces Vogel off the road and the band scraps every upcoming date.

eras.title: Pure Noise, and the founder comes back
eras.text: A new bassist, a new label, and then a surprise: Todd Jones, the founding guitarist who had left to start Nails, came back to produce. The pandemic made it Vogel and Jones alone in the studio.

years.h: Chris Linkovich of Cruel Hand replaces David Wood on bass
years.p: Linkovich had been filling in since April. The same year Terror moves to Pure Noise with the EP The Walls Will Fall.

years.h: Total Retaliation, produced by Will Putney
years.p: Terror's first Pure Noise album reaches 12 on Independent Albums, followed by a headlining run with Harm's Way, Backtrack and Year of the Knife.

years.h: Surprise EP Sink to the Hell on War Records
years.p: Four lost and unreleased Terror songs, dropped without warning.

years.h: Todd Jones comes back to produce Trapped in a World
years.p: Terror re-records songs from across its career for Good Fight, with founding guitarist Jones producing and playing guitar.

years.h: UFC fighter Khalil Rountree Jr. sings Out of My Face with Terror
years.p: The light heavyweight joins the band onstage at a California show and calls Terror Hall of Fame hardcore.

q: I turned Instagram off...lyrics started pouring out
years.src: Kerrang · Wikipedia: Terror · Wikipedia: Scott Vogel
years.h: Pain Into Power: Scott Vogel quits Instagram and the lyrics come
years.p: Stuck on lyrics, Vogel switched off social media and wrote six songs in two weeks. Todd Jones produced, and the pandemic kept the other members out of the studio.
years.xp: Released on Pure Noise, it reached number 8 on the German albums chart. The same year Vogel moved back home to Buffalo after two decades in Los Angeles.

eras.title: Still suffering, still touring
eras.text: Two decades in, Terror kept playing everywhere from Australia to Japan, Scott Vogel picked up a best-vocalist ranking, and Todd Jones produced another album.

years.h: On the road for Hatebreed's Rise of Brutality anniversary
years.p: Terror joins [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]]'s 20th anniversary tour for The Rise of Brutality.

q: I was a jock and I still am a jock.
years.h: Alternative Press names Scott Vogel hardcore's second-greatest vocalist
years.p: The same year Terror tours the world, from Australia with Kublai Khan to a short run in Japan.
years.xp: Vogel grew up in the Buffalo suburbs and still describes himself as a sports guy first. His step-brother brought home Run-D.M.C., punk and New York hardcore.

years.h: Europe with Gorilla Biscuits
years.p: Terror tours Europe with [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and Death Before Dishonor.

years.cap: A Deeper Struggle, dir. Derek Rathbun
years.h: A Deeper Struggle, a 20-minute Terror documentary
years.p: Derek Rathbun films Terror on its Latin America tour, released the day before the new album.

years.h: Still Suffer on Flatspot, produced by Todd Jones
years.p: Terror's first Flatspot album, mixed by Jon Markson, reaches 31 in Germany. The band tours North America with Pain of Truth and joins Hatebreed on Summer Slaughter.
